\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Even Moments}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.EvenMoments
\section{Overview}
Even-moment hypercontractivity controls noise from the second norm to every even integer norm. Fourier contraction, coordinate decompositions, and a finite-exponent duality principle supply related estimates.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier expansion of the squared norm of a noised function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_l2_fourier}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.parseval}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_l2_fourier}
Let $n\in\bbn$, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let
$\rho\in\bbr$. Write $T_\rho$ for the noise operator with parameter $\rho$,
$\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle$ for the $L^2$ inner product under the uniform
measure on $\{0,1\}^n$, and $\hat f(S)$ for the Fourier--Walsh coefficient of $f$ at
frequency $S\subseteq[n]$. Then
\[
  \langle T_\rho f,\, T_\rho f\rangle
  \;=\; \sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \bigl(\rho^{|S|}\bigr)^2\,\hat f(S)^2 .
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Contractivity of the noise operator in $L^2$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.contractivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_l2_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.parseval}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.contractivity}
Fix $n$, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be any Boolean function, and let $\rho\in\bbr$
satisfy $\rho^2\le 1$. Writing $T_\rho$ for the noise operator, so that $T_\rho
f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\rho^{|S|}\,\hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x)$, one has
\[
  \E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big]\;\le\;\E\big[f^2\big],
\]
where the expectation is taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. Here the Walsh characters are $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and the Fourier coefficients are $\widehat f(S)=\E[f\chi_S]$, with uniform expectation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[A bound on even binomial coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.binom_coeff_ineq}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.binom_coeff_ineq}
For every natural number $k \ge 1$ and every natural number $j$ with $j \le k$, the
inequality
\[
  \binom{2k}{2j} \;\le\; \binom{k}{j}\,(2k-1)^{j}
\]
holds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[$q$-th moment decomposition along the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.qth_moment_decomp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_boolCube_succ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformWeight_succ, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.qth_moment_decomp}
Let $q$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function.
Write $g$ for the average of $f$ over its last coordinate and $h$ for the
half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate, defined by
$g(x)=(f(x,0)+f(x,1))/2$ and $h(x)=(f(x,0)-f(x,1))/2$
on $\{0,1\}^n$.
Then the $q$-th moment of $f$ under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ decomposes as
\[
  \E[f^q] \;=\; \E\!\left[\frac{(g+h)^q + (g-h)^q}{2}\right],
\]
where the expectation on the right is taken over the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Moment decomposition of the noise operator across the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_qth_moment_decomp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_snoc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.qth_moment_decomp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{5}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_qth_moment_decomp}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, let $\rho\in\bbr$, and let $q$ be a
nonnegative integer. Write $A$ for the average of $f$ over its last coordinate and $D$
for the half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate, defined by
$A(x)=(f(x,0)+f(x,1))/2$ and $D(x)=(f(x,0)-f(x,1))/2$
on $\{0,1\}^n$.
Then the $q$-th moment of $T_\rho f$ over the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$
decomposes as
\[
  \E_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n+1}}\!\bigl[(T_\rho f)(x)^q\bigr]
= \E_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}}\!\left[\frac{\bigl(T_\rho A(x) + \rho\,T_\rho D(x)\bigr)^{q} +
\bigl(T_\rho A(x) - \rho\,T_\rho D(x)\bigr)^{q}}{2}\right],
\]
where on the right-hand side the noise operator acts on functions of $n$ variables. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[$(2, 2k)$-hypercontractivity for the noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.binom_coeff_ineq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_qth_moment_decomp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.second_moment_decomp, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\difficulty{7}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b003
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b007
}
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a real number $\rho$ with $\rho^2 \le \dfrac{1}{2k-1}$.
Then for every function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ on the Boolean hypercube,
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^{2k}\bigr] \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{k},
\]
where the expectation is taken under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$ and $T_\rho$ is
the noise operator $T_\rho f = \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \rho^{|S|}\,\hat f(S)\,\chi_S$.
Equivalently, $\norm{T_\rho f}_{2k} \le \norm{f}_2$. Here the Walsh characters are $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and the Fourier coefficients are $\widehat f(S)=\E[f\chi_S]$, with uniform expectation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$(2,q)$-hypercontractivity for even exponents]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_q}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b003,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_q}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b007
}
Let $q \ge 2$ be an even integer, and let $\rho \in \bbr$ satisfy $\rho^2 \le
\tfrac{1}{q-1}$. Then for every Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the noise
operator $T_\rho$ contracts from $L^2$ to $L^q$ in the sense that
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^q\bigr] \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{q/2},
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$L^2$ contractivity of the noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.contractivity, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2}
Let $\rho\in\bbr$ satisfy $\rho^2\le 1$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean
function. Then the noise operator $T_\rho$ does not increase the $L^2$ norm under the
uniform measure:
\[
  \E\!\left[(T_\rho f)^2\right] \;\le\; \E\!\left[f^2\right].
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A $(2,6)$-hypercontractive inequality for the noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_6}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_q, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{1}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_6}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b005,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p015-b003
}
Let $\rho\in\bbr$ satisfy $\rho^2\le \tfrac15$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be any
Boolean function. Then the sixth moment of the noised function $T_\rho f$ is controlled
by the cube of the second moment of $f$:
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^6\bigr] \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^3,
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$(2,2k)$-hypercontractivity in norm form]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p002-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b003
}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.hypercontractivity_2_2k_rpow}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p001-b004,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p011-b007
}
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a real noise rate $\rho$ satisfying $\rho^2 \le
\tfrac{1}{2k-1}$. Then for every Boolean function $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, the image
$T_\rho f$ under the noise operator obeys the $L^2$-to-$L^{2k}$ hypercontractive bound
\[
  \bigl(\E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^{2k}\bigr]\bigr)^{1/(2k)} \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{1/2},
\]
where the expectation is taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Self inner product equals expected square]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.innerProduct_eq_expect_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.innerProduct_eq_expect_sq}
For a Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the $L^2$ inner product of $f$ with
itself equals the expectation of its square: $\langle f, f\rangle = \E[f^2]$, that is,
$2^{-n}\sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} f(x)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the expected square of a smoothed Boolean function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_noiseOp_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_noiseOp_nonneg}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $\rho\in\bbr$ be arbitrary.
Applying the noise operator $T_\rho$ to $f$ and averaging the square over the uniform
measure gives a nonnegative quantity:
\[
  \E\!\left[(T_\rho f)^2\right]\;\ge\;0.
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of an expected absolute power]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function and let $p\in\bbr$ be any real exponent.
Using $0^0=1$ and $0^p=0$ for $p\ne0$, including negative $p$,
the expected value of $\abs{f}^p$ under the uniform measure on the hypercube is
nonnegative:
\[
\E\!\left[\,\abs{f}^{\,p}\,\right]\;=\;2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}\abs{f(x)}^{\,p}\;\ge\;0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Composition of noise operators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose}
For any real parameters $\rho,\sigma$ and any Boolean function
$f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, applying the noise operator $T_\sigma$ and then the noise
operator $T_\rho$ is the same as applying the single noise operator $T_{\rho\sigma}$;
that is,
\[
  T_\rho\bigl(T_\sigma f\bigr) \;=\; T_{\rho\sigma}\,f .
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

Let $1 < p$ and $q \ge 2$ be conjugate exponents, so that $1/p + 1/q = 1$, let $\rho \in
\bbr$, and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function; write $\norm{g}_r =
(\E[\abs{g}^r])^{1/r}$ for the $L^r$ norm under the uniform measure on the hypercube.
Suppose Hölder's inequality holds for the exponent pair $(p,q)$, that is, $\langle u,
v\rangle \le \norm{u}_p\,\norm{v}_q$ for all Boolean functions $u,v$, and suppose the
noise operator satisfies the $(2,q)$ bound $\E\bigl[\abs{T_\rho g}^q\bigr] \le
\bigl(\E[g^2]\bigr)^{q/2}$ for every Boolean function $g$. Then $T_\rho$ satisfies the
dual $(p,2)$ bound
\[
  \bigl(\E[(T_\rho f)^2]\bigr)^{1/2} \le \bigl(\E[\,\abs{f}^p\,]\bigr)^{1/p}.
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}
